text:
Anya Kumar: quick alert — onboarding open-7b-int4-v3: subtle token substitution after ~7k tokens in longctx harness. Not repeated phrases, single-token skew accumulating. Anyone on?

Diego Ramos: on it. single-token skew could be rotation misapply or key-slot misalignment. Which rope variant? fused or per-head?

Anya Kumar: --rope-mode=fused in these runs. Command: ./eval_longctx.sh --model open-7b-int4-v3 --ctx 16384 --quant int4 --rope fused --batch 1 --seed 7

Liu Chen: did you try fused vs scaled? fused has in-place interleaving math that sometimes interacts poorly with packed int4 kernels.

Anya Kumar: scaled runs look clean. Fused shows drift. Dumped logits at divergence point: step=186 token_idx=7124 top5 before->[0.42,0.21,0.08,0.06,0.05] next-step top1->0.14 unexpectedly

Sofie Hart: attach key/val checksum before+after prefill/inflight and layout: nibble-pair le or be?

Anya Kumar: KV_CHKSUM_PREFILL=0x7f3a2d KV_CHKSUM_INFLIGHT=0x7f3a2c — 1 mismatch. Layout=nibble-pair-le (current int4 packing).

Diego Ramos: 1-bit diff suggests single-bit shift during pack/unpack or rounding in int4 kernel. Did pack change recently? Liu?

Liu Chen: we switched to 2x4-bit pack stride opt in commit 9f8c3 last week to reduce stride on interleaved shards. Microbench but not longctx — could introduce carry when sequence crosses word boundary.

Anya Kumar: repro matrix: int4/fused/interleaved -> skew; int4/fused/single -> skew less frequent; int4/scaled/interleaved -> pass; float16/fused/interleaved -> pass. So int4+fused+interleave interaction.

Diego Ramos: hypothesis: pack_index calc off-by-one at word boundary. Add assert reconstruct nibbles==original for every pack/unpack roundtrip in prefill.

Anya Kumar: dev assert failed: pack_roundtrip_assert FAILED at token 7124: orig=0xA unpacked=0x8 -> nibble lost high bit. Points at shift/mask order bug.

Liu Chen: suspicious line pack_kernel.cu used wide 64-bit stores for perf; earlier we used per-nibble atomics. Interleaved sharding can make different writers update adjacent nibbles in same 64-bit word -> race.

Sofie Hart: good call. Forcing atomic nibble writes (slower) made fused/interleaved/int4 stable for 50/50 seeds locally -> confirms race.

Diego Ramos: plan: revert wide-store micro-opt, implement CAS loop that does 64-bit read-modify-write ensuring nibble correctness, add concurrency unit test simulating multiple writers hitting same word boundaries.

Liu Chen: PR fix/int4-pack-atomics switching to CAS loop. Bench: ~+0.8% CPU in prefill, token p99 unchanged.

ci-bot: CI started for fix/int4-pack-atomics — packing_concurrency unit test running.

Anya Kumar: local 1k-seed randomized sim -> no failures. Pushing gated MR. Added e2e longctx smoke fused+interleaved ctx=16384 500 randomized seeds -> no divergence so far.

Sofie Hart: after merge schedule 48h soak on dedicated pools and watch long-prompt customers. Tagging @eng-sre for rollout window.

Diego Ramos: add telemetry kv_prefill_pack_conflicts to surface CAS retries.

ci-bot: CI green: unit tests passed, smoke 500/500, perf nominal. MR: https://git.internal/redwood/rlib/pull/4902

Anya Kumar: merging MR now. Will monitor staging deploy and open incident-lite if anomalies. Thanks all.

Liu Chen: nice catch. Will include packing_concurrency test in onboarding harness.

Anya Kumar: closing thread.
